newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine to pick partner for car plant by May 1.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine to pick partner for car plant by May 1.

text.p: Ukraine will choose between General Motors (GM) of the United States and South Korea's Daewoo Group by May 1 for its investment partner in the AvtoZAZ car plant, a government press spokesman said on Friday.
"The government has ordered the commission to find a consultant by March 1 and to inform the government which investment project is better by May 1," the spokesman said.

An investment tender to find a strategic investor for AvtoZAZ was officially announced earlier this month. Economics Minister Vasyl Hureyev is heading a commission to oversee the tender, which has received proposals from GM and Daewoo.

Ukraine for two years has been seeking a strategic investor for AvtoZAZ, Ukraine's only car plant, in the eastern industrial city of Zaporizhya. Officials say the plant needs about $1 billion of investment over the next few years.
AvtoZAZ produced 6,881 small Tavria and Dana cars last year against 130,000 units in 1992. Its capacity is 150,000 units.
Tender rules require the investment partner to continue production of Ukrainian cars. Ukraine is in talks with both GM and Daewoo.
The size of the AvtoZAZ stake for sale is negotiable between 26 and 51 percent, government sources said.
They said GM foresaw two stages of restructuring. The first would see annual output of Opel Vectras rise to 25,000 per year, alongside production of 70,000-80,000 Tavrias.
Opel production would increase to 40,000 in a second stage.
Daewoo, which said in December it was ready to invest about $1 billion in AvtoZAZ, has proposed annual output of 100,000 Tavrias and assembly of three Daewoo models within 18 months.
The ministry for machine building, the military complex and conversion has asked the State Property Fund to replace AvtoZAZ's General Director, Olexander Sotnikov, UNIAN news agency said on Thursday.
Government sources said some top officials feared AvtoZAZ had been delaying the tender and that potential strategic investors might lose interest.
Ukrinform Business News agency said AvtoZAZ had also started talks with a group of Ukrainian banks on a $62.3 million credit in exchange for 20 percent of shares.
